solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Floor covering in vehicle, much liked

blocks.note: a car is a road vehicle
a pet is a favourite, someone much liked

explanation.surface: Someone admires the plush floor mats in their car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug laid over the whole floor of a room is the standard synonym for this textile.

clue.text: Bypass article on empty space

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another means it comes first, above the other

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a void is an empty space

explanation.surface: A road-planning note about a bypass built over waste ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go round it, steering clear of it, which is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tense here

blocks.note: first meaning: the grammatical tense for what is happening now
second meaning: in attendance, not absent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense here' reads as someone feeling nervous in a place; 'Tense' is the grammar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names the verb tense for now and also means in attendance, as at a roll call.

clue.text: Large number not turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A large crowd that failed to show up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred, or informally lots, is a common crossword sense for a large quantity.

clue.text: Impressive building in China attracting crowds, European, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so a china is a friend
first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A grand palace in China draws crowds of European tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is capitalised to look like the country, but it is Cockney rhyming slang for a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal residence is the archetypal grand, impressive edifice.

clue.text: Bird's role on trip, outside capital of Greece

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first, uppercase-sized letter
outside means one word wraps around the other letters

blocks.note: an actor's part is their role
a ride is a trip or journey
first letter of Greece

explanation.surface: A bird plays a part on a trip somewhere near Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Greece' looks like Athens but means only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a plump game fowl, the one in a pear tree in the carol.

clue.text: Failing in circuit, extremely strange

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme, outermost letters of the next word

blocks.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
first and last letters of strange

explanation.surface: A racing driver's strange mishap on one circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or momentary failure, as in a lapse of concentration.

clue.text: Assemble in religious building with English for time

indicators.note: with ... for means one letter is put in place of another

blocks.note: a convent is a house for nuns
E is the abbreviation for English
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: People gather in a church, with English spoken in place of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the end of CONVENT is swapped for E: 'English for time'.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to come together or call together for a meeting, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Person in authority reigning over Norway? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the following words is used, found inside them

blocks.note: letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A ruler with authority over Norway, though only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is an official who rules or administers a state or institution.

clue.text: Group of whales round northern body of water

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the next letter

blocks.note: a pod is a school of whales
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Whales gathering round a northern stretch of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond is a small, still stretch of water; facetiously the Atlantic too.

clue.text: Cutting part of blade move cautiously

blocks.note: first meaning: the sharp side of a knife
second meaning: to inch along slowly, as in creeping forward

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests handling a knife carefully; the two halves are separate meanings, a noun and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a knife's sharp side and the verb means to creep forward gradually.

clue.text: Bad errors involving church — one might have magic solution?

indicators.note: something bad is wrong, so these letters are put in a different order
involving means wrapping around and including other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Mistakes in church: is there a miracle fix for them?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' is a pun: not an answer to the errors but a liquid, a magic potion.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard might brew a potion, a magic liquid, so the question hints at the definition by example.

clue.text: Napkin I test — ever flexible

indicators.note: flexible letters can bend into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether a table napkin is pliable.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviette is the British word for a table napkin of cloth or paper.

clue.text: Dad's Conservative — snubbed minister

indicators.note: snubbed puns on snub-nosed: the word has its end cut short

blocks.note: Pa is Dad, so Dad's is Pa's
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Father, a Tory, was cold-shouldered by the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a clergyman in charge of a congregation, a church minister.

clue.text: A soldier states having no limits is trouble

indicators.note: having no limits means the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a GI is an American soldier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier declares that boundless something is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: STATES loses both outer letters. 'Trouble' is a verb here: to disturb or upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to disturb or worry someone, so it matches trouble as a verb.

clue.text: Unfortunately rude about street cleaner

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are disordered
about means going around the next letters

blocks.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A street sweeper is sadly impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street cleaner' wants to be read together; the street is wordplay and the definition is just 'cleaner'.
explanation.definitionFit: A duster is a cloth used to clean surfaces, so it is a cleaning item.

clue.text: Dubious new set-ups challenged at first

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
at first means taking only the opening letter of the word before

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of challenged

explanation.surface: Questionable new arrangements were disputed from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is open to doubt or mistrust, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Help rejected — group's bitter attack

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: aid is help
a tribe is a group of people

explanation.surface: Their offer of help refused, a group responds with a furious tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a forceful, angry verbal assault, a rant.

clue.text: Hint of openings for new goalkeepers in knockout game

indicators.note: openings for means the first letters of the words that follow
in means the letters are placed inside another word

blocks.note: a cup tie is a knockout match
first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Some sign of fresh goalies being blooded in a cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football a 'tie' is a single knockout cup match.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace or suggestion, as of colour or feeling.

clue.text: Inducement to protect a TV series

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so letters go inside

blocks.note: a sop is something given to placate or bribe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bribe offered to safeguard a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama, so the short form names a TV series.

clue.text: Entertain first-class person, inspiring

blocks.note: A is first class, as in A1 or A grade
a muse is a person who inspires an artist

explanation.surface: A top-notch, inspiring performer entertains.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse is to make someone laugh or keep them pleasantly occupied.

clue.text: Having brought in whiskey, criticise person easily manipulated

indicators.note: having brought in means the next word takes another letter inside it

blocks.note: to pan is to review harshly
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: After a drink, someone runs down a gullible stooge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is a chess piece, figuratively someone used by others for their own ends.

clue.text: Refined experience almost complete

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to have a taste of something is to experience it
full means complete

explanation.surface: A cultured experience that is nearly total.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteful means showing good aesthetic judgement, elegant, a near-synonym of refined.

clue.text: Source of light issuing at regular intervals

indicators.note: at regular intervals means taking every second letter of the word

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of issuing

explanation.surface: A lamp gives out light at steady intervals, like a lighthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Our star is the main source of daylight for the Earth.

clue.text: Calm, somewhat wiser, energetic

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is used, found within them

blocks.note: letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone described as peaceful, a little wiser and lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene describes being untroubled and tranquil, a close synonym.

clue.text: Spice fan, Margaret

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut
Meg is a pet form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret is mad about spices.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football slang a nutmeg is also kicking the ball through an opponent's legs, but here it is just the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of a tropical tree, grated as a kitchen spice.
